leading_positions.synthesis: Five members state B042 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clocks) as their preferred configuration. They share the two-name attribution (Katori for the magic-wavelength concept and first demonstration, Ye for record accuracy and stability near 1e-18), independent reproduction, and the view that the redefinition of the SI second should not delay recognition. They do not share a single wording: several ask for a citation anchored on the lattice-clock concept and its realisation rather than on frequency metrology in general, so that it is visibly separate from the 2005 comb prize. All five also record unresolved concerns about overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes and about lattice-clock groups outside the two names. Danielsson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce differ on alternatives (B057, B038, B019, B050, B028). Three other members, Eriksson, Johansson and Mehlig, list B042 as an alternative rather than their preferred prize.

Eriksson alone prefers B033 (dynamical mean-field theory; Georges, Kotliar, Vollhardt), on grounds of lasting influence, non-perturbative treatment of the Mott transition and testing against experiment. He himself acknowledges thin support, that DMFT may be read as a method rather than a discovery, that Metzner is outside the credited trio, that DFT+DMFT claims depend on double-counting and interaction-parameter choices, and that his own field proximity should be discounted. Olsson, in reply, regards the missing credit for the foundational step as decisive for this round while stating that this is not a verdict on the merit of the framework.

Johansson alone prefers B038 (Cirac, Zoller, Blatt; trapped-ion gates and quantum simulation), citing the proposal-to-realisation chain and breadth of influence, while conceding that B042 is cleaner on attribution. Others (Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce, Eriksson) raise the same difficulties he does: overlap with the 2012 prize, the claims of Wineland and Monroe who are not in the credited names, and a label that bundles ion computing with cold-atom simulation. Johansson also discloses a possible bias against B038 arising from his superconducting-circuit platform.

Mehlig alone prefers B019 (magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene; MacDonald, Bistritzer, Jarillo-Herrero), emphasising a quantitative prediction followed by experiment and a new tunable many-body platform, with the three-name limit mapping onto theory plus experiment. He accepts that the field is young, the pairing mechanism is unsettled, results depend on twist-angle disorder and sample quality, and the junior experimentalists and other moire theorists are not credited. He states that B042 is his fallback if B019 is judged premature. Others (Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce) list B019 as an alternative or ask for patience on maturity.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members agree that B042 is a mature, reproducible result with a clean two-name attribution; five prefer it, and the other three (Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig) list it as an alternative.

Members who discuss B057 (Danielsson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce, Eriksson) agree that the Higgs discovery is scientifically overdue and mature, and that the obstacle is the credit to Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee, not the physics.

Several members (Kroll, Lindroth, Pearce, Danielsson) state that any B042 citation should name the magic-wavelength lattice concept and its realisation so as not to duplicate the 2005 frequency-comb prize.
Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce see overlap with 2012 as a real difficulty for B038, and several note the bundling of ion computing with cold-atom simulation.

Most members who touch on timing (Danielsson, Lindroth, Pearce, Olsson in part) agree that the pending redefinition of the SI second is a policy step and does not by itself justify delaying B042; Eriksson treats it as the reason he lists B042 as an alternative rather than his preferred prize.
scientific_disputes: Whether the lattice clock is a distinct invention or an application of the toolbox honoured in 2005 (frequency combs) and 2012 (single trapped-ion control). Eriksson, Mehlig and Danielsson raise this; Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce argue that the magic-wavelength scheme with many atoms is separable. Mehlig adds that Ye's accuracy work leans on comb technology.
Whether DMFT (B033) is a discovery or a method and approximation scheme (Eriksson himself raises this, Olsson presses it).

Whether the B038 scope can be drawn narrowly (gate proposal and its realisation as a computational resource) or whether it unavoidably merges ion computing and cold-atom simulation, where B050 is already on the shortlist.

Whether an unresolved pairing mechanism and sample dependence in B019 weigh against recognition; Mehlig argues that the criterion is the discovery, not a closed theory of its origin, as with superconductivity.
attribution_disputes: B057: the three credited names are founding leaders of ATLAS and CMS, which Danielsson, Eriksson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce read as crediting instrument creation and leadership rather than the discovery analyses of thousands; Danielsson calls it a policy choice about collaboration credit.

B042: other lattice-clock groups (Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow, Takamoto and others) are outside the two names, and Katori's early-proposal priority has not been checked against the record by Danielsson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson or Pearce, all of whom state they cannot verify it in detail.
B033: Metzner is outside the credited trio, although the infinite-dimension limit was the first step (Eriksson).
B019: junior experimentalists who led the first measurements and earlier moire-band theorists are outside the three names (Eriksson, Kroll, Mehlig).
B038: Wineland and Monroe, not in the credited names, have claims on ion gates (Johansson, Pearce, Kroll, Lindroth).
maturity_disputes: B019 is about eight years old; Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth and Olsson ask for more time, while Mehlig regards waiting a few years as not costless.
B042: Eriksson regards the unreached redefinition of the second as a reason recognition could wait; Danielsson, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce state that the confirmed science is the relevant test.
B049 (circuit QED): timing relative to the 2025 prize is raised by Johansson, Mehlig and Lindroth as a redundancy concern, together with how four names would be reduced to three.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Olsson: first-ranked B028 (aberration-corrected electron microscopy) is in her own research field and she led the International Federation of Societies for Microscopy, so she will recuse from deliberating on it and has not made it her preferred configuration.

Olsson: documented University of Tokyo and JSPS fellowships and exchanges with Japanese universities, flagged for B042 because Katori is at Japanese institutions; no personal or collaborative tie to Katori or Ye is documented.

Johansson: directs WACQT at Chalmers and works on superconducting circuits, so he would consider recusal or restraint on B049 and discloses a possible bias against B038 because of the competing superconducting platform.
Olsson and Johansson are both at Chalmers, and Olsson states she will not treat his assessment of circuit QED as independent of that setting.

Kroll: doctoral-period research stay in John Hall's laboratory (2005 prize context relevant to B042) and Lund and WACQT quantum-technology connections relevant to B038; no documented collaboration with Katori or Ye; he invites the committee to judge whether recusal is needed.

Lindroth: long-running collaboration with Anne L'Huillier and the Lund attosecond group, not involving Katori or Ye; she asks that shared-publication links be checked before any vote if B050 or B049 advance, and discloses general atomic-physics familiarity.
Eriksson: field proximity to B033 (DFT and DMFT-adjacent methods) and, less so, B019, which he says he discounts.

Pearce (chair): no recorded tie to the B042 community; general experience of large detector collaborations and accelerator-based physics bears on B057 without a recorded tie to ATLAS, CMS or the credited names.
questions_for_round2: Can a B042 citation be worded around the magic-wavelength lattice concept and its realisation at the 1e-18 level so that it is clearly separate from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and does Ye's comb and ultrastable-laser work remain separable? Kroll is asked whether the stability gained from interrogating many atoms simultaneously is the decisive point of separation.

What does the documentary record show about the early lattice-clock proposal and first demonstration, and do Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow, Takamoto or others hold priority claims that a two-name credit cannot accommodate? No member has verified this in detail.

Is the committee prepared to adopt a convention for crediting large-collaboration discoveries, so that B057 can be given a defensible three-name form; if not, is B057 excluded for this round, and what would a citation recognising detector concepts and leadership have to say?

Can B038 be scoped to the gate proposal and its experimental realisation so as not to duplicate 2012, how are Wineland and Monroe to be treated, and should the cold-atom simulation work be left to B050?
Should the pending redefinition of the SI second delay a B042 prize (Eriksson) or is it a policy step independent of the science (Danielsson, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce)?
Is B019 mature enough now (Mehlig) or should it wait, given the open pairing mechanism, sample dependence, and the omission of the junior experimentalists and early moire theorists?

Can Eriksson and Olsson resolve whether a DMFT citation could be framed around the concept and the impurity mapping within the three credited names, given the omission of Metzner, or does B033 remain a method-versus-discovery question?

Which disclosed connections (Olsson on B028 and Japanese institutions, Johansson on B049 and B038, Kroll on Hall and WACQT, Lindroth on the Lund attosecond group) require recusal or restraint on a specific ballot in round 2?
summary.chair_observation: The explicit round-1 positions are concentrated on B042, with five members preferring it and three single-member dissenting preferences (B033, B038, B019) that all list or defer to it as fallback or alternative. The remaining questions are about the wording and priority record of B042, the treatment of collaboration credit for B057, the scope of B038 against 2012, and the maturity of B019. These are for the committee to resolve in round 2; this summary is not a ruling.
